name: MD-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+39 partisan lean makes a Republican win historically implausible
Incumbent Glenn Ivey has a large financial edge, with no reported fundraising for his challenger
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 98%
Green Party candidate on the ballot may slightly trim the Democratic margin
model.rationale: This is one of the most Democratic-leaning House seats in the country, and Ivey returns as the incumbent with roughly $483,000 on hand against a Republican challenger showing no measurable fundraising or outside support. With no general-election polling and no competitive ratings, the fundamentals and market pricing both point to an overwhelming Democratic win.
model.watch: Only an unexpected, district-wide scandal or collapse in Democratic turnout below presidential-low levels would put the seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Maryland's 4th District is a deeply Democratic seat, with a partisan lean of D+39, and incumbent Glenn Ivey is running for reelection with the advantages that come with holding the seat. He has raised about $855,000 and holds roughly $483,000 in cash, while Republican nominee George McDermott shows no reported fundraising or outside backing.

The district's fundamentals, the lopsided financial picture, and prediction markets pricing a Democratic win near 98% all align. The main uncertainty is the size of the margin rather than the outcome, and a Green Party candidate on the ballot could modestly reduce Ivey's share. Everything points to a comfortable Democratic hold in November.
